pr.taskz: 与 PHP 相同的 loop 逻辑，用 JavaScript 写：返回 1 至 n 中同时是 3 和 5 倍数的数目。

pr.tz: 用 JavaScript 做 linear search
pr.task: Translate the PHP flag search into JavaScript: write function findIndex(arr, target) that uses a while loop with a found flag and returns the index of target, or -1 if it is not in the array.
pr.taskz: 把 PHP 的 flag 搜寻改写成 JavaScript：返回 target 的 index，找不到返回 -1。

sec: 3.4 Accessing client-sent data in server-side script
3.7 Chapter Task – Building a Quadratic Equation Solver

cards.t: Recap: a PHP file and its resulting HTML
cards.tz: 回顾：PHP 文件与结果 HTML
cards.en:
A PHP file is stored on the web server. When a client requests it, the server executes the PHP code and generates a resulting HTML file, which is sent back to the client in an HTTP response. The browser only ever receives the resulting HTML; it never sees the PHP source code. This is why PHP is called a server-side scripting language.

In Chapter 2, PHP pages were generated from data written inside the script itself. In this chapter the server-side script becomes interactive: it receives data sent by the client (what the user typed or chose in a web page) and uses that data to build a personalised response. Key idea to memorise: the client sends input in an HTTP request; the server processes it with PHP and returns HTML in an HTTP response.
cards.zh:
PHP 文件存放在 web server 上。客户端请求它时，服务器执行 PHP 代码，生成结果 HTML（resulting HTML），再通过 HTTP response 返回。浏览器只收到结果 HTML，永远看不到 PHP 源码，所以 PHP 是 server-side scripting language。

第 2 章的 PHP 只用脚本内写死的数据生成网页；本章开始让脚本接收客户端送来的数据（用户输入或选择的内容），再按这些数据生成个性化的回应。要背的一句：the client sends input in an HTTP request; the server processes it with PHP and returns HTML in an HTTP response。

ex.q: A user opens hello.php which contains <p><?php echo 3+4; ?></p>. What does the browser receive if it views the page source?
ex.a:
The server runs the PHP block first, so the browser receives only 
<p>7</p>
The PHP code itself is never sent to the client.
ex.az: 服务器先执行 PHP，浏览器只收到 <p>7</p>，看不到 PHP 代码。

cards.t: Receiving user input in a web application
cards.tz: Web 应用如何接收用户输入
cards.en:
Whenever a user types into a textbox or clicks a button, the user is providing data to the web application. The browser submits this data to the server, the server processes it and returns a response (an HTML page).

Example: on a search engine, the user types "5-star hotels" and clicks Search. The browser sends the search term to the server, the server looks it up in its database and generates a result page.

This chapter covers three linked steps:
  • HTML forms collect the input in the browser.
  • The form data is sent using an HTTP request method, either GET or POST.
  • The PHP script reads the data through superglobals ($_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE), validates it, and generates the response.
cards.zh:
用户在文本框输入或点击按钮，就是在向 web 应用提供数据。浏览器把数据 submit 到服务器，服务器处理后返回回应（HTML 网页）。

例：在搜索引擎输入 "5-star hotels" 再按 Search，浏览器把关键词送到服务器，服务器查数据库后生成结果页。

本章三个环节：
  • 用 HTML forms 在浏览器收集输入；
  • 用 HTTP request method（GET 或 POST）发送表单数据；
  • PHP 通过 superglobals（$_GET、$_POST、$_COOKIE）读取数据，validate 后生成回应。

ex.q: Describe what happens, from the client's side to the server's side, when a user searches for "5-star hotels".
ex.a:
1. The user types the keyword into a text field of an HTML form and clicks the submit button.
2. The browser puts the keyword into an HTTP request and sends it to the server.
3. The server-side script reads the keyword, searches the database and generates an HTML results page.
4. The page is returned in an HTTP response and displayed by the browser.
ex.az: 用户输入并提交 → 浏览器把关键词放进 HTTP request → 服务器脚本读取、查数据库、生成结果 HTML → HTTP response 返回浏览器显示。

cards.en:
Frameworks are pre-written, standardised software libraries that provide tools and guidelines to build web applications more efficiently.

Examples:
  • Laravel: a PHP framework
  • Django: a Python framework
  • Vue and React: JavaScript frameworks for the front end
Benefits:
  • They provide pre-built code for common tasks (forms, validation, database access, login), so developers do not need to "reinvent the wheel" and the development cycle is shorter.
  • They are standardised, so the code written by a team is consistent and easier to maintain.
In this book you write raw PHP to understand how things work underneath; in industry, frameworks usually handle form processing and validation for you.
cards.zh:
Frameworks are pre-written, standardised software libraries，提供工具和规范，令 web 应用开发更有效率。

例子：Laravel（PHP）、Django（Python）、Vue / React（JavaScript 前端）。

好处：
  • 提供常见功能的预建代码（表单、验证、数据库、登入），不用 reinvent the wheel，缩短开发周期；
  • 标准化，团队代码 consistent and maintainable。
课本让你直接写 PHP 去理解底层原理；业界通常用框架处理表单和验证。

ex.q: A start-up wants to build an online shop quickly with a small team using PHP. Suggest a suitable tool and give two benefits.
ex.a:
Use a PHP framework such as Laravel.
(1) It provides pre-built, tested code for common features such as forms, validation and database access, which shortens development time.
(2) It is standardised, so all team members write code in a consistent way that is easier to maintain.
ex.az: 建议用 Laravel：预建代码缩短开发时间；标准化令代码一致、易维护。

cards.zh:
HTML 表单由 <form>…</form> 定义。form 本身没有外观，但 all input elements must be placed within the form tag pair，只有在 form 里面的字段会一起提交。

两个重要属性：
  • action：specifies the location to send the form's data，通常是服务器上的 PHP 文件；
  • method：用 GET 还是 POST 发送。
省略 method → 默认 GET；action="" → 送到当前页面同一 URL。

ex.q: Write the opening tag of a form that sends its data to login.php so that the data is not shown in the address bar.
ex.a:
<form action="login.php" method="POST">
POST puts the data in the request body, so it does not appear in the URL.
ex.az: 用 POST，数据放在 request body，不显示在地址栏。

cards.t: Input fields and the text field
cards.en:
An input field allows users to input data into an HTML form. Most fields are created with the <input> tag and its type attribute. This chapter uses: text, password, date, dropdown (select), checkbox and submit (examples also use type="number").

A text field allows users to enter text into it. It is the most basic input field:
Your Nickname:
<input type="text" name="nickname">
The words "Your Nickname:" are ordinary text shown to the user as a label; they are not submitted.

Important: <input> is an empty element and does not have a closing tag. Writing </input> is wrong. In contrast, <form>, <select> and <option> do need closing tags.
cards.zh:
An input field allows users to input data into an HTML form. 多数字段用 <input> 加 type 属性建立。本章：text、password、date、dropdown (select)、checkbox、submit（例子中也用到 number）。

A text field allows users to enter text into it. 前面的 "Your Nickname:" 只是显示给用户的说明文字，不会提交。

注意：<input> 是空元素，没有结束标签，写 </input> 是错的；而 <form>、<select>、<option> 需要结束标签。

ex.q: Spot the error: Name: <input type="text" name="n"></input>
ex.a:
<input> has no closing tag, so </input> should be removed:
Name: <input type="text" name="n">
ex.az: <input> 没有结束标签，删去 </input>。

cards.en:
The name attribute gives the field an identifier. The user cannot see it, but it is used when the form's data are sent to the server: the name becomes the index and the user's input becomes the value.

Rules and good practice:
  • Always define name for every <input> and <select>. A field with no name is not submitted at all, so the server script cannot read it.
  • Use a descriptive name such as full_name, password, email.
  • The PHP script must use exactly the same name as the index: $_POST["full_name"]. Names are case-sensitive in PHP array indexes.
Exam answer: Form data are submitted in index-value pairs. The name attribute is used as the index while the user-inputted data are the value. Without it the server-side script cannot access the data.
cards.zh:
The name attribute gives the field an identifier. 用户看不到，但提交数据到服务器时使用：name 成为 index，用户输入成为 value。
  • 每个 <input>、<select> 都要有 name；没有 name 的字段不会被提交，服务器读不到。
  • 用有意义的名字，如 full_name、email。
  • PHP 中 index 必须完全一致：$_POST["full_name"]（区分大小写）。
考试答法：Form data are submitted in index-value pairs; the name attribute is the index and the user input is the value.

ex.q: A form has <input type="text" id="email"> and the PHP page uses $_POST["email"], but always gets nothing. Explain and fix.
ex.a:
The field has an id but no name. Only fields with a name are submitted, so there is no index "email" in $_POST. Fix:
<input type="text" id="email" name="email">
ex.az: 只有 id 没有 name，字段不会提交；加上 name="email"。

cards.en:
<input type="text" name="eng_name" required>

The boolean attribute required forces the user to fill in the field. If the field is empty when the user clicks submit, the browser blocks the form submission and alerts the user (e.g. "Please fill in this field").

This is an example of client-side validation: the check happens in the browser before any data is sent. It improves user experience and reduces invalid requests, but it can be bypassed (old browser, developer tools editing the HTML, or a request sent without the form), so the server must still check the data (presence check with empty()/isset()).

Note that required has no value; writing just required is enough.
cards.zh:
required 是布尔属性：forces the user to fill in the field。若提交时为空，浏览器阻止提交并提示用户。

这是 client-side validation：在数据送出前于浏览器检查，改善体验、减少无效请求；但可被绕过（旧浏览器、developer tools 改 HTML、直接发请求），所以服务器仍需检查（用 empty()/isset() 做 presence check）。写 required 就够，不用给值。

ex.q: Make a password field that cannot be left blank.
ex.a: <input type="password" name="pw" required>
ex.az: 加 required。

cards.en:
A password field obscures the user's input when displayed on screen. It is used for sensitive data such as passwords or PINs so that people nearby cannot read what is typed.
Password: <input type="password" name="pw">
Characters appear as dots or asterisks. Browsers differ: some briefly show the last character typed, some show a button to reveal the password.

Common misunderstanding: a password field only hides the characters on screen. It does not encrypt the data. The value is submitted like any other field. If the form uses GET, the password will appear in the URL in plain text. So a login form should use POST, and the site should use HTTPS to encrypt the transmission.
cards.zh:
A password field obscures the user's input when displayed on screen. 用于密码、PIN 等敏感数据，旁人看不到输入内容（显示为圆点/星号）。不同浏览器做法不同（短暂显示最后一个字、提供显示按钮）。

常见误解：它只是屏幕上遮盖，没有加密，提交时跟普通字段一样。若表单用 GET，密码会以明文出现在 URL。所以登入表单应用 POST，网站要用 HTTPS 加密传输。

ex.q: A login form uses method="GET" and <input type="password" name="pw">. The user types 1234. What appears in the address bar after submitting to home.php (other field: username=amy)?
ex.a:
home.php?username=amy&pw=1234
The password field hid the characters on screen only; GET still places the value in the query string. Use POST instead.
ex.az: password 只在画面遮盖；GET 仍把 pw=1234 放进 URL。应改用 POST。

cards.en:
A date field is used specifically to input a date. The browser shows a calendar picker, so choosing a date is easier and less prone to error; only valid dates can be entered.
Birthday: <input type="date" name="bday">
The value submitted to the server is a string in the format yyyy-mm-dd, e.g. 2010-03-15.

min and max constrain the range of dates allowed (enrichment):
<input type="date" name="bday" min="2022-12-20" max="2022-12-27">
Because PHP generates HTML, the limit can be dynamic. To allow only today or later dates:
<input type="date" name="d" min="<?php echo date("Y-m-d"); ?>">
min/max are client-side only, so the server should still do a range check.
cards.zh:
A date field is used specifically to input a date. 浏览器显示日历，选择容易、less prone to error，只能输入有效日期。提交的值是 yyyy-mm-dd 格式字符串。

min 与 max 限制可选日期范围（Enrichment）。因为 PHP 可以生成 HTML，可用 min="<?php echo date("Y-m-d"); ?>" 令用户只能选今天或以后。min/max 只是客户端限制，服务器仍要做 range check。

ex.q: A booking form must only accept dates in December 2026. Write the field.
ex.a: <input type="date" name="book_date" min="2026-12-01" max="2026-12-31">
ex.az: 用 min/max，格式 yyyy-mm-dd。

cards.en:
A dropdown selection field provides pre-defined choices. It simplifies input and reduces the chances of error, because the user can only pick from the list. By default only one option can be chosen.
Region:
<select name="region">
  <option value="HK">Hong Kong Island</option>
  <option value="KL">Kowloon</option>
  <option value="NT">New Territories</option>
</select>
Key points:
  • The name goes on <select>, not on each option.
  • <select> and <option> both need closing tags.
  • The value attribute is what is submitted to the server; the text between the option tags is what the user sees.
  • If value is omitted, the text between <option> and </option> is submitted.
Benefit of defining value: shorter codes compatible with the server's database, making server-side validation and processing easier.
cards.zh:
A dropdown selection field provides pre-defined choices. 简化输入、reduces the chances of error，默认只能选一项。
  • name 写在 <select>，不写在 option；
  • <select>、<option> 都要结束标签；
  • value = 提交给服务器的值；标签之间的文字 = 用户看到的文字；
  • 省略 value → 提交标签之间的文字。
定义 value 的好处：可用较短、与数据库一致的代码，方便服务器验证和处理。

ex.q: The user chooses "Kowloon" in the select above. What index-value pair is submitted? What if the options had no value attributes?
ex.a: With value: region=KL. Without value: the displayed text is submitted, region=Kowloon.
ex.az: 有 value 提交 region=KL；没有 value 则提交 region=Kowloon。

cards.en:
Checkboxes allow users to submit multiple values for a single field. Each checkbox is a separate <input> element (unlike a dropdown, which is one element).
Interests:
<input type="checkbox" name="interest[]" value="code"> Coding
<input type="checkbox" name="interest[]" value="cook"> Cooking
<input type="checkbox" name="interest[]" value="music"> Music
Rules:
  • All checkboxes for the same question must share the same name.
  • The name must be postfixed with square brackets [] so PHP collects the values into an array.
  • The value is what is sent when that box is ticked.
In PHP, $_POST["interest"] (no brackets in the index) is an array, e.g. ["code","music"]. Unticked boxes send nothing; if no box is ticked, the index does not exist at all, so check with isset() first. Without [], only the last ticked value would be kept.
cards.zh:
Checkboxes allow users to submit multiple values for a single field. 每个 checkbox 是独立的 <input>。
  • 同一问题的 checkbox 必须同一个 name；
  • name 后面要加 []，PHP 才会收集成数组；
  • value = 勾选时送出的值。
PHP 中 $_POST["interest"]（index 不加 []）是数组。没勾的不会送出；一个都没勾时该 index 不存在，要先 isset()。没有 [] 的话只会保留最后一个勾选值。

ex.q: A user ticks Coding and Music above. Write PHP to print "You chose 2 interests" and handle the case of no ticks.
ex.a:
<?php
if(isset($_POST["interest"])){
  $n = count($_POST["interest"]);
  echo "You chose {$n} interests";
} else {
  echo "You chose no interests";
}
?>
$_POST["interest"] is ["code","music"], so count() gives 2.
ex.az: $_POST["interest"] 是数组 ["code","music"]，count 得 2；没勾时 index 不存在，所以先 isset。

cards.en:
The submit button sends the form's data to a server for processing. When clicked, the browser collects all named fields in the form and sends them in an HTTP request to the form's action location using its method.
<input type="submit" name="submit" value="Find Out Now!">
  • The value attribute changes the text displayed on the button (default text is browser-dependent, e.g. "Submit").
  • By convention it has name="submit". Then the button itself is also submitted as an index-value pair (submit=Find Out Now!).
This is useful: the index "submit" only exists if the user clicked the button, so a page can test isset($_POST["submit"]) to know whether the form was actually submitted (used in the Quadratic Equation Solver).
cards.zh:
The submit button sends the form's data to a server for processing. 点击后浏览器把 form 内所有有 name 的字段，按 method 发到 action。
  • value 改变按钮上显示的文字；
  • 惯例 name="submit"，按钮本身也会作为 index-value 对提交。
用途：只有用户点击了按钮，index "submit" 才存在，所以可用 isset($_POST["submit"]) 判断表单是否真的提交过。

ex.q: Write a submit button showing "Calculate BMI" that can be detected in PHP.
ex.a:
<input type="submit" name="submit" value="Calculate BMI">
PHP: if(isset($_POST["submit"])){ ... }
ex.az: value 改文字，name 令它可被检测。

cards.tz: Number 字段与 step 属性
cards.en:
<input type="number" name="height"> lets the user type only a number (with up/down spinner arrows on many browsers).

The step attribute specifies the granularity that the inputted value must adhere to.
  • Default step is 1, so only whole numbers are accepted; entering 81.3 would be blocked by the browser.
  • step="0.1" accepts one decimal place.
  • step="any" accepts any real number, e.g. GPA values or decimal coefficients like -2.5 in the Quadratic Equation Solver.
min and max can also be used with number fields, e.g. min="0" max="250". All of these are client-side checks; the value still arrives at the server as a string and must be validated with is_numeric() and range checks.
cards.zh:
type="number" 只能输入数字。

step specifies the granularity the inputted value must adhere to.
  • 默认 step=1 → 只接受整数，输入 81.3 会被浏览器拦下；
  • step="0.1" 接受一位小数；
  • step="any" 接受任何实数（如 GPA、二次方程的小数系数）。
也可配 min、max。这些都是 client-side 检查；数值到服务器时仍是字符串，要用 is_numeric() 和 range check 验证。

ex.q: Weight is entered in kg with decimals, from 0 to 250. Write the field.
ex.a:
<input type="number" name="weight" step="any" min="0" max="250">
Without step="any", 81.3 would be rejected because the default step is 1.
ex.az: 默认 step=1 只收整数，所以要 step="any"。

cards.t: Example 3.1 method: building a form from a wireframe
cards.tz: 例 3.1 方法：按 wireframe 建表单
cards.en:
To turn a wireframe (a sketch of the form) into HTML, go field by field and pick the right type:
  1. Free text (name, nickname) → type="text"
  2. Hidden on screen (password) → type="password"
  3. A date → type="date"
  4. One choice from a fixed list → <select> with <option value=...>
  5. Several choices allowed → checkboxes sharing one name with []
  6. Numbers → type="number" (with step="any" if decimals allowed)
  7. Mandatory fields → add required
  8. Finish with a submit button.
Then set the form's action (which PHP file processes it) and method (GET or POST). Every field needs a name. For dropdowns, define short values (e.g. "HK") that match the server's database.
cards.zh: 把 wireframe 变成 HTML：逐个字段选类型：自由文字 → text；要遮盖 → password；日期 → date；固定清单单选 → select/option；可多选 → checkbox（同名加 []）；数字 → number（有小数加 step="any"）；必填 → required；最后加 submit。再设 form 的 action 和 method。每个字段都要 name；下拉选项用与数据库一致的短 value。

ex.q: Wireframe: Full name (text, required); Password; Date of birth; Form class (5A/5B/5C); Clubs (Chess, Robotics, Drama; may pick several); button "Join". Data goes to join.php.
ex.a:
<form action="join.php" method="POST">
 Full name: <input type="text" name="full_name" required><br>
 Password: <input type="password" name="pw"><br>
 Date of birth: <input type="date" name="dob"><br>
 Class: <select name="cls">
  <option value="5A">5A</option>
  <option value="5B">5B</option>
  <option value="5C">5C</option>
 </select><br>
 Clubs:
 <input type="checkbox" name="club[]" value="chess"> Chess
 <input type="checkbox" name="club[]" value="robot"> Robotics
 <input type="checkbox" name="club[]" value="drama"> Drama<br>
 <input type="submit" name="submit" value="Join">
</form>
POST is chosen because a password is sent and a record will be created.
ex.az: 逐项选类型；含密码且会新增记录 → POST。

cards.t: Submitting a form: the four steps
cards.en:
When the user clicks submit, the browser does four steps:
  1. Organise the data into index-value pairs: the name attribute is used as the index and the data inputted by the user becomes the value (e.g. name→Andy, height→179, weight→81.3, submit→submit).
  2. Prepare an HTTP request using the form's attributes: action gives the location, forming the Request URL (domain + file on the server); method gives the HTTP request method (GET or POST). Form data are always sent through an HTTP request.
  3. Add the form data to the request: for GET it is encoded into the URL as a query string; for POST it is placed in the request body.
  4. Send the request from the client to the server.
Tips: method omitted → GET; action="" → sent to the same URL as the current page.
cards.zh:
点击 submit 后浏览器做四步：
  1. 整理成 index-value pairs：name 作 index，用户输入作 value；
  2. 准备 HTTP request：action 组成 Request URL（域名 + 服务器文件），method 决定 HTTP request method。Form data are always sent through an HTTP request.
  3. 把数据加入请求：GET → 编码进 URL 成为 query string；POST → 放入 request body；
  4. 由客户端把请求发到服务器。
Tip：省略 method → GET；action="" → 送到当前页面同一 URL。

ex.q: Form on https://mysite.net/myBMI.html: action="resultBMI.php", method="GET". User enters name Andy, height 179, weight 81.3. Give the request URL.
ex.a:
https://mysite.net/resultBMI.php?name=Andy&height=179&weight=81.3&submit=submit
(assuming the submit button has name="submit" value="submit").
ex.az: 按 action 组成 URL，GET 把 index=value 用 & 接在 ? 之后。

cards.en:
With GET, form data is encoded into the request URL. This part of the URL is called the query string.
https://mysite.net/resultBMI.php?name=Andy&height=179
  • It starts with ? after the file path.
  • Each pair is written index=value.
  • Pairs are separated by &.
Because it is part of the URL, the query string can also be typed or edited by hand, which is one reason the server must validate everything it receives.

Special characters are encoded by the browser (e.g. a space becomes + or %20, @ becomes %40). A checkbox array appears as repeated indexes such as lang%5B%5D=en&lang%5B%5D=zh (%5B%5D is []).

With POST, the same pairs are in the request body, separate from the URL, so they are not limited by URL length.
cards.zh: GET 时表单数据编码进 URL，这部分叫 query string：以 ? 开始，每对写成 index=value，以 & 分隔。因为在 URL 里，用户可自己手动修改，所以服务器必须验证。特殊字符会被编码（空格→+ 或 %20，@→%40；checkbox 数组显示为 lang%5B%5D=…）。POST 则把同样的 pairs 放在 request body，不受 URL 长度限制。

ex.q: pastPaper.php?year=2022&subject=english : list the index-value pairs and the PHP to read the subject.
ex.a: Pairs: year→"2022", subject→"english". $subject = $_GET["subject"];
ex.az: 两对：year=2022、subject=english，用 $_GET 读取。

cards.t: Misconception: who chooses GET or POST?
cards.tz: 误解：谁决定 GET 或 POST？
cards.en:
Misconception: the user decides whether data is sent by GET or POST when clicking submit.

Fact: the web developer makes that decision, through the method attribute of the <form> tag. The user normally does not see or choose it. If the developer leaves out method, the browser uses GET.

The developer should choose based on the purpose of the request (fetching vs changing data), the sensitivity of the data, whether the result should be bookmarkable, and the size/type of data. A user with developer tools could edit the form's method, which is another reason the server-side script should check what it receives (e.g. use isset() before reading $_POST).
cards.zh:
误解：用户按 submit 时决定用 GET 还是 POST。
事实：由 web developer 决定，通过 <form> 的 method 属性；用户一般看不到也不选。省略 method 则默认 GET。开发者按目的（取资料 vs 改资料）、敏感度、能否 bookmark、数据大小/类型来选。用户可用 developer tools 改 method，所以服务器要先 isset() 再读 $_POST。

ex.q: A form tag is <form action="s.php">. Which method is used and who decided it?
ex.a: GET, because method is omitted and GET is the default. The developer decided it (by leaving it out), not the user.
ex.az: 省略 method → GET，由开发者决定。

cards.tz: GET 与 POST 的意图
cards.en:
GET: the client wants to retrieve (fetch) a specific resource from the server. The query string describes which resource is wanted. Example: filtering TVs in an online shop by brand, size and price; no changes are made to the server's database.

POST: the client submits information to perform a specific action, often effecting a change in the server's state, such as creating or editing a record. Example: booking a flight adds a new booking record to the database.

Analogy from the book: a bank with a single counter serves different requests (deposit, withdraw) according to what the ticket says; in the same way one PHP file can handle GET and POST requests differently.

Enrichment: GET is often described as idempotent: sending the same GET request multiple times should not alter the server's state. In practice, how the server handles a request depends on its implementation.
cards.zh:
GET：客户端想从服务器取得某个资源，query string 描述要哪个资源，例如网店按品牌、尺寸、价格筛选电视，不改动数据库。
POST：客户端提交信息以执行某个动作，常会改变服务器状态（新增/修改记录），例如订机票新增预订记录。
类比：银行单一柜台按票据提供不同服务 → 同一 PHP 文件可分别处理 GET 和 POST。
Enrichment：GET 是 idempotent：同一 GET 请求发多次不应改变服务器状态（实际取决于实现）。

ex.q: Classify: (i) searching courses by keyword, (ii) submitting an online order, (iii) checking a stock price.
ex.a: (i) GET: retrieves matching courses, no change. (ii) POST: creates an order record, changes the server's state. (iii) GET: fetches data only, and the URL can be bookmarked.
ex.az: 检索 → GET；新增记录 → POST。

cards.t: GET vs POST: visibility, bookmarks and history
cards.tz: GET 与 POST：可见性、书签、历史
cards.en:
Visibility: in GET the query string is part of the URL, so the data is visible on the browser's address bar. In POST the request body is not visible to the user.

Bookmark / history: a GET URL with its query string can be bookmarked and saved in browsing history, and can be copied and shared (e.g. sharing a YouTube link sends the same GET request when clicked). POST requests cannot be bookmarked or saved in history in general.

Therefore sensitive data such as passwords and ID numbers should be sent with POST; with GET it would show up like home.php?username=amy&pw=20100521 and stay in history.

Misconception: GET data is exposed on the network because it is in the URL. Fact: if HTTPS is used, all data in an HTTP request, including the request URL, are encrypted during transmission. The real risk of GET is the address bar, history and bookmarks.
cards.zh:
可见性：GET 的 query string 是 URL 一部分，显示在地址栏；POST 的 request body 用户看不到。
书签/历史：GET URL 可 bookmark、存入浏览历史、可复制分享；POST 一般不能。
所以密码、身份证号等敏感数据用 POST。
误解：GET 数据在网络上会暴露。事实：用 HTTPS 时，整个 HTTP request（包括 URL）在传输时都加密；GET 的风险在地址栏、历史和书签。

ex.q: A teacher wants students to share a link that opens the search result for "2022 English" past papers. GET or POST? Why?
ex.a: GET: the query string is part of the URL, so the result page can be bookmarked and shared; the request only retrieves data.
ex.az: GET 可 bookmark 和分享。

cards.t: GET vs POST: size, data type and caching
cards.tz: GET 与 POST：大小、数据类型、缓存
cards.en:
Length limit: URLs have a maximum length, so a GET query string cannot exceed a specified size (2KB in most cases). POST has no size limit on the request body.

Data type: GET can carry only text data, no binary data. POST can include binary data such as images and files (file uploads need POST).

Caching: the response to a specific GET request can be cached, so frequently used URLs load faster. A proxy server can store popular pages and return the cached copy directly, reducing the web server's load and loading time (Chapter 6). POST responses are generally not cached because each request body differs.

Book error: the Summary table in the book prints the POST column the same as GET for some rows; follow the main text (POST: no size limit, binary allowed, not cached).
AspectGETPOST
PurposeFetch resourcePerform action / change state
Data locationQuery string in URLRequest body
VisibleYes (address bar)No
Bookmark/historyYesNo
Size~2KBNo limit
BinaryNoYes
CachedCan beGenerally not
cards.zh:
长度：GET 的 query string 不能超过约 2KB；POST 无大小限制。
数据类型：GET 只能文字；POST 可含图片、文件等二进制数据（上传文件要用 POST）。
缓存：GET 回应可被 cache，proxy server 可直接返回缓存页，减轻服务器负担、加快载入；POST 一般不 cache，因每次 body 不同。
课本勘误：Summary 表 POST 一栏部分误印成与 GET 相同，以正文为准。

ex.q: A user uploads a 3 MB profile photo. Which method, and give two reasons.
ex.a: POST. (1) GET can only carry text data; a photo is binary data. (2) GET is limited to about 2KB, while POST has no size limit.
ex.az: POST：GET 只能文字且约 2KB 上限。

cards.t: Example 3.2 method: choosing GET or POST
cards.tz: 例 3.2 方法：选择 GET 或 POST
cards.en:
Decision checklist for each form or request:
  • Will it create or change a record on the server (booking, order, registration, posting a comment)? → POST.
  • Does it contain sensitive data such as login credentials or ID numbers? → POST (not shown in the address bar, not saved in history/bookmarks).
  • Does it upload files or large data? → POST.
  • Does it only retrieve/search/filter data (course search, stock price, menu list)? → GET, which also allows bookmarking, sharing and caching.
One application can use both: login uses POST, then searching uses GET. In an exam, always state the method and link the reason to the scenario (e.g. "the user may want to bookmark the search result").
cards.zh:
判断清单：
  • 会新增/修改服务器记录？→ POST
  • 含敏感数据（登入资料、身份证号）？→ POST
  • 上传文件或大量数据？→ POST
  • 只是检索/搜索/筛选？→ GET（可 bookmark、分享、cache）
同一应用可混用：登入 POST、搜索 GET。考试要写出方法并把理由连到情境。

ex.q: A cinema site: (a) search films by date; (b) log in; (c) buy tickets. Choose methods.
ex.a: (a) GET: retrieves showtimes only; result can be bookmarked/shared. (b) POST: password is sensitive and must not appear in the URL/history. (c) POST: creates a ticket order record, changing the server's state.
ex.az: (a) GET；(b) POST 敏感；(c) POST 改服务器状态。

cards.t: Server side of the request-response cycle
cards.en:
After the user submits a form, the server accesses the data sent by the client, processes the data, and returns a response. For a POST request to resultBMI.php:
  1. The server uses the request URL to locate the requested file (resultBMI.php).
  2. Because a PHP file is requested, the server gathers all data in the request body into the associative array $_POST.
  3. The PHP code uses the values through $_POST (e.g. calculates the BMI).
  4. The resulting HTML is generated and returned in an HTTP response.
For GET the same happens, but the query string data is gathered into $_GET.

These arrays are called superglobals: built-in variables that are always available in every PHP script without declaring them. Their indexes are the name attributes of the form fields.
cards.zh: 用户提交后，服务器读取客户端数据、处理、返回回应。POST 到 resultBMI.php：①按 URL 找到文件；②因为是 PHP，把 request body 的数据收集到关联数组 $_POST；③PHP 通过 $_POST 使用数值；④生成 HTML 用 HTTP response 返回。GET 则收集到 $_GET。这些叫 superglobals：每个 PHP 脚本都可直接用的内建变量，index 就是表单字段的 name。

ex.q: Body of a POST request: name=Andy&height=179&weight=81.3&submit=submit. Show the contents of $_POST.
ex.a:
IndexValue
"name""Andy"
"height""179"
"weight""81.3"
"submit""submit"
All values are strings.
ex.az: $_POST 四对，值都是字符串。

cards.en:
$_POST is a superglobal associative array: all data in the request body of a POST request are gathered into $_POST. $_GET does the same for the query string of a GET request.
<?php
  $name = $_POST["name"];
  if($_POST["marks"] > 80){
    $grade = "A";
  }
?>
<?php // pastPaper.php?year=2022&subject=english
  $subject = $_GET["subject"];
  if($_GET["year"] < 2012){
    echo "No past paper before 2012!";
  }
?>
Points:
  • Use the array that matches the form's method: a POST form's data is not in $_GET.
  • The index must match the field's name exactly; for a checkbox named lang[] use $_POST["lang"].
  • All values arrive as strings ("179", not 179). PHP converts numeric strings automatically in arithmetic and comparison, but you should still type-check with is_numeric().
cards.zh:
$_POST 是 superglobal 关联数组：POST 请求 body 的所有数据收集到 $_POST；$_GET 收集 GET 请求的 query string。
  • 要用对应 method 的数组：POST 表单的数据不在 $_GET；
  • index 要与 name 完全一致；checkbox lang[] 用 $_POST["lang"]；
  • 所有值都是字符串；PHP 算术/比较时会自动转换数字字符串，但仍要用 is_numeric() 检查。

ex.q: URL: score.php?eng=72&maths=88. Write PHP that echoes the average.
ex.a:
<?php
$avg = ($_GET["eng"] + $_GET["maths"]) / 2;
echo "Average: {$avg}";
?>
Output: Average: 80
ex.az: 用 $_GET，"72"+"88" 自动转成数字，得 80。

cards.t: Using $_POST values inside strings and calculations
cards.tz: 在字符串和计算中使用 $_POST
cards.en:
To put an array element inside a double-quoted string, wrap it in curly braces {}:
echo "Hi {$_POST["name"]}, your BMI is {$bmi}.";
Alternatively use concatenation: echo "Hi " . $_POST["name"];

Calculations work directly on numeric strings. Weighted average (Checkpoint 3.3 style):
$gGPA = ($_POST["gpa_1"] + $_POST["gpa_2"]
      + $_POST["gpa_3"] * 1.5 + $_POST["gpa_4"] * 2)
      / (1 + 1 + 1.5 + 2);
Useful functions: round($x, 1) rounds to 1 decimal place; ** is the power operator ($h ** 2); sqrt() gives a square root.
cards.zh: 双引号字符串中嵌入数组元素，用 {} 包住："Hi {$_POST["name"]}"，或用 . 连接。计算可直接用数字字符串（如加权平均）。常用：round($x,1) 四舍五入到 1 位小数；** 乘方；sqrt() 开方。

ex.q: gpa_1..gpa_4 = 3.0, 3.6, 3.2, 3.5 with weights 1,1,1.5,2. Compute $gGPA.

cards.en:
BMI = weight (kg) / height (m)². The book's app uses two files:
  • myBMI.html: an HTML form with action="resultBMI.php" method="POST", fields name, height (cm), weight (kg) and a submit button.
  • resultBMI.php: reads $_POST, validates, calculates and displays the BMI, or shows "Invalid data entered!".
<?php
$valid = true;
if(empty($_POST["name"])){ $valid = false; }
if(empty($_POST["height"])){ $valid = false; }
elseif($_POST["height"] < 0 || $_POST["height"] > 250){ $valid = false; }
if(empty($_POST["weight"])){ $valid = false; }
elseif($_POST["weight"] < 0 || $_POST["weight"] > 250){ $valid = false; }
if($valid){
  $bmi = $_POST["weight"] / ($_POST["height"]/100) ** 2;
  $bmi = round($bmi, 1);
  echo "Hi {$_POST["name"]}, your BMI is {$bmi}.";
  if($bmi < 18.5){ echo " Underweight"; }
  elseif($bmi > 25){ echo " Overweight"; }
  else { echo " Normal"; }
} else {
  echo "Invalid data entered!";
}
?>
Height is in cm, so divide by 100 to get metres.
cards.zh: BMI = 体重(kg) / 身高(m)²。两个文件：myBMI.html（表单，action="resultBMI.php"，POST）和 resultBMI.php（读 $_POST、验证、计算、显示，或输出 "Invalid data entered!"）。身高以 cm 输入，要 ÷100 变米；** 是乘方。分类：<18.5 underweight，>25 overweight，其余 normal。

ex.q: Andy: height 179, weight 81.3. What is printed?
ex.a:
BMI = 81.3 / 1.79² = 81.3 / 3.2041 ≈ 25.37 → round to 25.4. Since 25.4 > 25: 
Hi Andy, your BMI is 25.4. Overweight

cards.en:
Data validation prevents invalid user-inputted data from being used. A web app can validate in two places.

Client-side validation implements the validation mechanism on the client's browser, using HTML form controls (required, min, max, step, type) and JavaScript. The browser validates the input before the data are sent to the server; if anything is invalid it alerts the user and sends nothing.
Advantages: prevents most invalid data from being sent, reduces the workload on the server, saves time for the user (instant feedback).
Disadvantages: may perform unpredictably: old browsers may not support some attributes, JavaScript may be disabled, and it can be bypassed.

Server-side validation implements the validation mechanism on the server with server-side scripts (e.g. PHP if-statements). The server validates data after it is sent: invalid → returns a page with an error message; valid → processes it (calculation, database) and returns a success page. Some checks can only be done on the server, e.g. checking whether a username has already been taken (needs the database).
cards.zh:
Client-side validation：在浏览器实现，用 HTML 属性（required、min、max、step）和 JavaScript，数据送出前检查。优点：挡下大部分无效数据、减轻服务器负担、为用户节省时间。缺点：可能表现不可预期（旧浏览器、关掉 JS）、可被绕过。
Server-side validation：在服务器用脚本实现，数据送到后检查，无效 → 返回错误页；有效 → 处理并返回成功页。有些检查只能在服务器做，如用户名是否已被使用。

ex.q: For a registration form, give one check suited to the client side and one that must be on the server.
ex.a: Client side: presence check that the email field is filled in (required). Server only: checking that the username is not already registered, because it needs to look up the server's database.
ex.az: 客户端：required；服务器：查数据库看用户名是否已用。

cards.t: Misconception: validation is one or the other; always validate on the server
cards.en:
Misconception: client-side and server-side validation are alternatives; a site uses one or the other.
Fact: client-side and server-side validation are always used in parallel. They have the same purpose; the difference is only where the mechanism is implemented.

Principle: all client-sent data should be validated on the server side, regardless of whether client-side validation has been used. Reasons client-side checks can be bypassed:
  • The user opens the browser's developer mode and edits the HTML (removes required, changes option values) or the JavaScript.
  • A hacker sends HTTP requests containing fabricated data directly to the URL, without using the form at all.
  • JavaScript is disabled or the browser is outdated.
  • Typing the URL or refreshing sends a GET request with no form data.
cards.zh:
误解：client-side 和 server-side 二选一。事实：两者总是并用，目的相同，只是实现位置不同。
原则：所有客户端数据都应在服务器验证，不论有没有客户端验证。因为客户端检查可被绕过：developer mode 改 HTML/JS；黑客直接向 URL 发送伪造数据的 HTTP request；JS 被关；直接输入 URL/刷新发出无数据的 GET。

ex.q: A dropdown only offers delivery days 1–5. A user still submits delivery=9. How, and how should the server respond?
ex.a: The user edited the option value with developer tools (or sent a fabricated request). The server should run a fixed-value check, e.g. if(!in_array($_POST["delivery"], [1,2,3,4,5])){ $valid = false; }, and return an error page.
ex.az: 改 HTML 或伪造请求；服务器用 in_array 检查。

cards.zh: 书中服务器验证用 flag 变量：先设 true；任何检查失败就设 false；最后按 flag 决定处理或报错。用 if…elseif：先 presence check，存在才做 range check。BMI：Name → presence；Height/Weight → presence + range (0–250)。

ex.q: Trace: $_POST = ["name"=>"Bo","height"=>"300","weight"=>"60"]. What is $valid at the end?
ex.a: name not empty → stays true. height not empty, but 300 > 250 → $valid = false. weight is fine but cannot reset it to true. Final: false, so "Invalid data entered!" is printed.
ex.az: 身高 300 超范围 → false，之后不会变回 true。

cards.en:
FunctionReturns true when
isset($x)the variable exists in runtime and is not null, whatever its value (even "")
empty($x)the variable does not exist in runtime, or is empty ("", "0", 0, null, false, empty array)
Both are used before accessing $_GET/$_POST elements, and neither causes an error if the index does not exist.

Why the index may not exist: resultBMI.php expects a POST request, but if the user types its URL or refreshes the page, a GET request is sent, so $_POST is empty and $_POST["name"] gives an undefined index runtime warning/error. It also happens when the HTML form has been altered on the client side (by the user or a browser extension), or when no checkbox is ticked. Good practice: always check whether an element exists before using it.

Trap: empty("0") is true, so a presence check with empty() rejects a legitimate input of 0. To allow 0 use isset($x) && $x !== "".
cards.zh:
isset()：变量存在且非 null 即 true（"" 也算）。empty()：变量不存在或为空即 true（""、"0"、0、null、false、空数组）。两者都不会因 index 不存在而报错。
为何 index 可能不存在：用户直接输入 URL 或刷新 → GET 请求，$_POST 为空，直接访问会 undefined index；表单被客户端修改；checkbox 一个都没勾。好习惯：使用前先检查是否存在。
陷阱：empty("0") 为 true，输入 0 会被当作没填；要允许 0 用 isset($x) && $x !== ""。

ex.q: For each value of $_POST["b"], give isset() and empty(): (i) "5" (ii) "" (iii) "0" (iv) index missing.
ex.a: (i) isset true, empty false. (ii) isset true, empty true. (iii) isset true, empty true. (iv) isset false, empty true.
ex.az: "0" 也被 empty 视为空。

cards.t: Validation functions: presence, fixed value, type
cards.en:
CheckFunctionReturns true when
Presenceempty($v)missing or empty
Fixed valuein_array($v, $arr)$v is one of the elements of $arr
Typeis_numeric($v)a number or numeric string
Typeis_string($v)a string
Lengthstrlen($s)(returns number of characters)
Formatstrpos($s, $sub)(returns position or false)
Fixed value check:
$accepted = ["A","B","C"];
if(!in_array($_GET["ans"], $accepted)){ $valid = false; }
Good for dropdown values, since a user could edit the options. in_array uses loose comparison by default, so "3" matches 3.

Type check:
if(!is_numeric($_POST["age"]) || $_POST["age"] <= 0){ $valid = false; }
is_numeric("81.3"), is_numeric("-5") → true; is_numeric("abc"), is_numeric("12abc") → false. Note: $_POST values are always strings, so is_string() is almost always true (except array fields such as checkboxes).
cards.zh: 常用验证函数：presence → empty()；fixed value → in_array($v,$arr)（适合检查 dropdown 值，默认宽松比较，"3" 等于 3）；type → is_numeric()（"81.3"、"-5" 为 true，"abc"、"12abc" 为 false）、is_string()（$_POST 值本来都是字符串，几乎总是 true，checkbox 数组例外）；length → strlen()；format → strpos()。

ex.q: Write a check that the submitted grade is A, B, C or D and the age is a positive number.
ex.a:
$valid = true;
if(!in_array($_POST["grade"], ["A","B","C","D"])){ $valid = false; }
if(!is_numeric($_POST["age"]) || $_POST["age"] <= 0){ $valid = false; }
ex.az: in_array 做固定值检查；is_numeric + 范围。

cards.t: Length and format checks: strlen() and strpos()
cards.en:
Length check: strlen() returns the number of characters of the given string.
if(strlen($_POST["uid"]) > 20){ $valid = false; }
Format check: strpos() returns the position of the first occurrence of a substring; if it is not found, it returns false. Positions start at 0.
if(!strpos($_POST["email"], "@")){ $valid = false; }
Subtle point: if "@" is at position 0, strpos returns 0 and !0 is true, so the email is also rejected. For emails this happens to be correct (an email cannot start with @), but to test strictly for "not found" write strpos($s, "@") === false.

Examples: strlen("Hello") = 5; strpos("amy@x.com","@") = 3; strpos("amy","@") = false.
cards.zh:
strlen() 返回字符串字符数（length check）。strpos() 返回子字符串首次出现的位置，找不到返回 false，位置从 0 开始（format check）。
细节：@ 在第 0 位时返回 0，!0 为 true → 也判无效（对 email 合理）。严格判断找不到用 === false。例：strlen("Hello")=5；strpos("amy@x.com","@")=3。

ex.q: A user ID must be 4 to 12 characters. Write the check.
ex.a:
$len = strlen($_POST["uid"]);
if($len < 4 || $len > 12){ $valid = false; }
ex.az: 用 strlen 和 || 检查上下限。

cards.t: Date range check and loop presence check
cards.tz: 日期 range check 与循环 presence check
cards.en:
Date range check: date("Y-m-d") returns today's date as a yyyy-mm-dd string, the same format a date field submits. Strings in this fixed format compare correctly (alphabetical order = time order):
if($_POST["eat_out"] > date("Y-m-d")){
  $valid = false;   // date in the future is not allowed
}
Presence check with a loop: to check many expected fields at once, store their names in an array and loop:
$valid = true;
$fields = ["name", "age", "email", "submit"];
foreach($fields as $f){
  if(empty($_POST[$f])){ $valid = false; }
}
Purpose: check that every expected field is present (not empty) in the POST request; any missing one makes $valid false. This is shorter and easier to maintain than one if-statement per field.
cards.zh:
日期 range check：date("Y-m-d") 返回今天的 yyyy-mm-dd 字符串，与 date 字段格式一致，可直接比较大小（字典序=时间序）。
循环 presence check：把字段名放进数组，foreach 逐个 empty() 检查，任何一个缺失 → $valid=false。比逐个写 if 更短、易维护。

ex.q: Today is 2026-11-25. Is $valid false for eat_out = "2026-11-30"? For "2026-01-05"?
ex.az: 同格式字符串比较即日期先后。

cards.en:
A Cookie is a small text file stored by a website on the client's browser. Its content is in key-value (index-value) pairs, and it is usually associated with a specific domain and an expiration date.

Uses:
  • Maintaining user preferences (language, theme)
  • Tracking user behaviour (analytics)
  • Persistent authentication (staying logged in via a session ID)
So websites can show personalised content, remember logins and keep shopping-cart items.

Because Cookies are sent back to the server with every request to the domain, the server can give a personalised experience without storing the data in its own database.
cards.zh: A Cookie is a small text file stored by a website on the client's browser. 内容是 key-value pairs，通常与特定 domain 和到期日关联。用途：保存用户偏好、追踪用户行为、持续登入；可提供个性化内容、记住登入、保留购物车。因为 cookie 每次请求都送回服务器，服务器不用把这些数据存在自己的数据库也能提供个性化体验。

ex.q: Give two pieces of data an English-learning site could reasonably store in Cookies.
ex.a: (1) The user's preferred interface language, e.g. lang=zh. (2) The last lesson searched, so it can be shown for quick access.
ex.az: 语言偏好、最近搜索记录。

cards.t: How a Cookie is created and read
cards.en:
Creating / changing:
  1. The server receives a request and runs the PHP script.
  2. A set-cookie header is attached to the HTTP response, stating the Cookie's name (index) and value, e.g. university = HKU.
  3. Upon receiving the response, the browser creates the Cookie and stores it locally.
To change a value, the server sends a new set-cookie header with the same name, which overwrites the old value. In PHP this is done with setcookie("university", "HKU", time()+86400*30); (must be called before any HTML output).

Reading: in every subsequent HTTP request, all Cookies created by this domain are attached to the request. The server reads them with the superglobal $_COOKIE:
<?php
if(isset($_COOKIE["university"])){
  echo "Welcome back, {$_COOKIE["university"]} fan!";
}
?>
cards.zh:
建立/修改：①服务器收到请求，执行 PHP；②在 HTTP response 加上 set-cookie header，写明 cookie 的 name 和 value；③浏览器收到后建立 cookie 并存在本地。修改：再发同名 set-cookie 覆盖旧值。PHP 用 setcookie(name, value, expiry)（要在任何 HTML 输出之前）。
读取：之后每个 HTTP request 都会附上该 domain 的所有 cookie，服务器用 superglobal $_COOKIE 读取（先 isset）。

ex.q: Explain how a server knows a returning user prefers Traditional Chinese.
ex.a: On a previous visit the server sent a set-cookie header (e.g. lang=zh-hk) in the HTTP response and the browser stored it. On the next visit the browser attaches this Cookie to the HTTP request, and the PHP script reads $_COOKIE["lang"] and outputs the page in Traditional Chinese.
ex.az: 上次以 set-cookie 存下，之后每次请求附上 cookie，用 $_COOKIE 读取。

cards.en:
The browser only sends the Cookies associated with the current domain. Therefore data in Cookies can only be read or modified by the domain that issued the Cookie. A Cookie set by shop.com is never sent to news.com.

Within the same domain, the request for any URL (any page or PHP file on that domain) carries the same Cookies, so a preference set on one page can be used on every page of the site.

Exam answer for "why can a server use data stored on the client?": Cookies set by a domain are sent to the server in every HTTP request to that domain, so server-side scripts can access them via $_COOKIE. To set or change a Cookie, the server sends the index and value in the set-cookie header of an HTTP response.
cards.zh:
浏览器只送出与当前 domain 相关的 cookie → cookie 的数据只能被发出它的 domain 读取或修改。同一 domain 下任何 URL 的请求都带相同 cookie，所以在一页设定的偏好全站可用。
考试答法：Cookies set by a domain are sent to the server in every HTTP request to that domain, so server-side scripts can access them via $_COOKIE.

ex.q: shop.com sets cart=3items. The user then visits shop.com/pay.php and news.com. Which requests carry the Cookie?
ex.a: Only the request to shop.com/pay.php, because it is the same domain. news.com never receives it.
ex.az: 只有同 domain 的请求会带。

cards.t: Benefits and potential risks of Cookies
cards.en:
Benefits (better user experience):
  • Saving the language preference
  • Saving the last search record for faster access
  • Saving filtering criteria on an online shop
  • Keeping shopping-cart items
Analytics / market research: how often a user visited the site, how long a user spent on a page.

Potential problems, because Cookies live on the client:
  • The value may be altered by the user or a browser extension.
  • The Cookie may be deleted (browsers clear them for privacy, or the user does).
  • Cookies may be disabled entirely, so the browser ignores set-cookie headers.
  • Size limit of about 4KB, since every Cookie is sent with every request; only a few thousand characters.
So the server should isset()-check and validate $_COOKIE values just like form data.
cards.zh:
好处：保存语言偏好、最近搜索、网店筛选条件、购物车；做分析（访问次数、停留时间）。
风险（因为存在客户端）：值可能被修改；被删除；被完全停用，浏览器忽略 set-cookie；约 4KB 大小限制（每次请求都要传）。所以 $_COOKIE 也要 isset() 和验证。

ex.q: A site stores the theme colour in a Cookie but some users always see the default theme. Give two possible reasons.
ex.a: (1) The user has disabled Cookies, so the set-cookie header is ignored. (2) The browser deletes Cookies regularly (or the user cleared them), so the value no longer exists.
ex.az: 停用 cookie；cookie 被删除。

cards.en:
Any sensitive data should not be saved in Cookies.
Ill-considered useProblem
Storing the user ID to identify who is logged inAnyone can edit the Cookie and pretend to be another user
Storing credit card detailsMay not be properly encrypted and could be leaked
Storing an in-game currency balanceCan be edited with browser tools to cheat
Rule of thumb: store only harmless preferences in Cookies; keep important data (balances, permissions, personal data) in the server's database and, if needed, store only a random session ID in the Cookie.
cards.zh: 敏感数据不应存在 cookie。存 user ID → 任何人改 cookie 就能冒充别人；存信用卡 → 可能未加密而外泄；存游戏货币余额 → 用浏览器工具修改作弊。原则：cookie 只放无害偏好；重要数据放服务器数据库，cookie 里最多放随机 session ID。

ex.q: A game stores coins=500 in a Cookie and reads $_COOKIE["coins"] when buying items. Identify the problem and suggest an improvement.
ex.a: Problem: the Cookie is on the client, so the player can edit it (e.g. coins=999999) with browser tools and buy items for free. Improvement: store the balance in the server's database linked to the account, and keep only a session ID in the Cookie.
ex.az: 余额可被改；应存数据库。

cards.en:
Session: a session allows a user to remain logged in when navigating between multiple web pages. At each login a random session ID is generated and saved both in the client's Cookie and in the server's database. When the client sends a request with a valid session ID, the server cross-checks it with the database to identify the user. (In PHP: session_start() and $_SESSION; the data stays on the server, only the ID is in the Cookie.) This is a key idea in account-based web apps.

localStorage: a modern web API used by client-side JavaScript. Its data is not sent to the server with every request, so it has a much larger storage capacity and supports app-like (PWA) experiences.
Misconception: localStorage replaces Cookies. Fact: Cookies are still used extensively for servers to manage sessions; the two are used together.
cards.zh:
Session：令用户在多个网页之间保持登入。每次登入生成随机 session ID，同时存于客户端 cookie 和服务器数据库；请求带有效 ID 时服务器对照数据库确认身份。（PHP：session_start()、$_SESSION。）
localStorage：客户端 JavaScript 用的 API，数据不随每个请求送到服务器，所以容量大得多，支持 PWA。误解：localStorage 取代 cookie。事实：服务器仍大量用 cookie 管理 session。

ex.q: Why is storing a session ID in a Cookie safer than storing the user ID?
ex.a: A user ID is short and guessable, so editing it lets someone impersonate another user. A session ID is a long random value that the server checks against its database; a made-up value will not match any valid session.
ex.az: session ID 随机且由服务器核对，难以伪造。

cards.en:
The chapter task builds a web app that solves ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0).

Discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac:
  • Δ > 0: two distinct real roots
  • Δ = 0: one repeated real root
  • Δ < 0: no real root
Roots: x = (−b ± √Δ) / (2a); repeated root x = −b / (2a).

In PHP: $b ** 2 for b², sqrt($d) for the square root. Parentheses around (2 * $a) are essential: -$b / 2 * $a would compute (−b/2)×a.
cards.zh: 本章任务：解 ax²+bx+c=0（a≠0）。判别式 Δ=b²−4ac：Δ>0 两个不同实根；Δ=0 一个重根；Δ<0 无实根。根 x=(−b±√Δ)/(2a)。PHP：$b ** 2、sqrt()；(2*$a) 的括号必须有，否则 -$b/2*$a 会变成 (−b/2)×a。

ex.q: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0 using the discriminant.
ex.a: a=1, b=−5, c=6. Δ = 25 − 24 = 1 > 0 → two distinct real roots. x = (5 ± 1)/2 → 3 and 2.

ex.q: Classify x² + 2x + 5 = 0.
ex.a: Δ = 4 − 20 = −16 < 0 → no real root.
ex.az: Δ<0 无实根。

cards.t: Quadratic Solver: one page, two kinds of request
cards.tz: Quadratic Solver：同一页处理两种请求
cards.en:
quadraticSolver.php is a single file containing:
  • Part A: the HTML form, with action="" and method="POST"; fields a, b, c are type="number" step="any".
  • Part B: data validation (presence + type checks).
  • Part C: calculating and displaying the solutions.
action="" sends the form back to the same page, so results appear under the form.

Two cases:
  • Case 1: first visit (typing the URL) → GET request, no form data → show only the form.
  • Case 2: clicking submit → POST request with a, b, c and submit.
The index "submit" only exists if the user clicks the submit button, so:
if(isset($_POST["submit"])){
  // Part B and Part C
}
handles both cases without an undefined-index error.
cards.zh:
quadraticSolver.php 一个文件包含：Part A 表单（action=""，POST，a/b/c 用 number + step="any"）；Part B 验证；Part C 计算。action="" 令结果显示在同页表单下。
Case 1：首次访问 → GET，无表单数据 → 只显示表单。Case 2：按 submit → POST。只有按了 submit，index "submit" 才存在，所以用 isset($_POST["submit"]) 区分两种情况。

ex.q: Why not test isset($_POST["a"]) instead of submit? Is either OK?
ex.a: Both indexes appear only after the form is submitted by POST, so either works in normal use. The book tests "submit" because it clearly means "the user clicked the button", independent of which data fields exist.
ex.az: 两者正常情况都可；submit 表达"用户按了按钮"更清晰。

cards.t: Quadratic Solver Part B and Part C code
cards.tz: Quadratic Solver Part B / C 代码
cards.en:
if(isset($_POST["submit"])){
  $valid = true;
  if(empty($_POST["a"]) || !is_numeric($_POST["a"])){
    $valid = false;
  }elseif(empty($_POST["b"]) || !is_numeric($_POST["b"])){
    $valid = false;
  }elseif(empty($_POST["c"]) || !is_numeric($_POST["c"])){
    $valid = false;
  }
  if($valid){
    $a = $_POST["a"]; $b = $_POST["b"]; $c = $_POST["c"];
    $d = $b ** 2 - 4 * $a * $c;
    if($d > 0){
      $r1 = (-$b + sqrt($d)) / (2 * $a);
      $r2 = (-$b - sqrt($d)) / (2 * $a);
      echo "There are two distinct real solutions.<br>";
      echo "x = {$r1} or x = {$r2}";
    }elseif($d == 0){
      $r = -$b / (2 * $a);
      echo "There is one repeated real solution.<br>x = {$r}";
    }else{
      echo "There is no real solution.";
    }
  }else{
    echo "Invalid input!";
  }
}
|| is logical OR, ! is NOT. Limitation: because empty("0") is true, a = 0 is rejected (correct, since a ≠ 0), but b = 0 or c = 0 is also rejected even though x² − 4 = 0 is valid. Improvement: check b and c with !isset(...) || $_POST["b"] === "" instead of empty().
cards.zh: Part B 用 empty() || !is_numeric() 做 presence + type check；Part C 用判别式分三种情况输出。|| 是 OR，! 是 NOT。局限：empty("0") 为 true，所以 a=0 被拒（正确），但 b=0 或 c=0 也会被拒（如 x²−4=0 本来有效）。改善：b、c 改用 !isset() || === "" 检查。

ex.q: Trace with a=1, b=0, c=−4.
ex.a: empty("0") is true, so the b-check sets $valid = false and the page prints "Invalid input!" even though the roots are ±2. This shows the limitation of empty().
ex.az: b=0 被 empty 判为空 → Invalid input!，这是 empty() 的局限。

cards.t: Generating form fields with PHP loops
cards.tz: 用 PHP 循环生成表单字段
cards.zh: PHP 能生成 HTML，所以可用循环输出大量字段（如点名 checkbox）。双引号字符串内的 " 要写成 \"。处理端：用 in_array 找出没被勾选的学号，$absent[] = $i 把元素加到数组末尾；in_array 宽松比较令整数 3 等于字符串 "3"。没人被勾时 present 不存在，要先 isset。

ex.q: $no_of_stud = 5 and the boxes for 1, 2, 4 are ticked. What is $absent?
ex.a: $present = ["1","2","4"]. Loop i = 1..5: 3 and 5 are not in the array → $absent = [3, 5].
ex.az: 没勾的 3 和 5。

cards.zh: 检查输入是否在一列已存的值中（激活码、已注册 email），用线性查找 + flag：foreach 比较，相同则 $found=true。快捷写法 in_array()。Email 注册：先 strpos 做 format check，再循环比较已注册 email，相同 → $valid=false。实际清单在服务器数据库，所以只能在服务器检查。

ex.q: $registered = ["amy@a.com","bob@b.com"]; user enters "bob@b.com". Trace the check.
ex.a: Format: strpos returns 3 (truthy) → passes. Loop: "amy@a.com" ≠; "bob@b.com" == → $valid = false: "Email already registered".
ex.az: 格式通过，但在清单中 → 无效。

mc.q: Where is the PHP code in a .php file executed?
mc.e: PHP is server-side: the server runs it and sends the resulting HTML.

mc.q: Which of the following does the browser receive when it requests a PHP page?
o: The resulting HTML generated by the server
mc.e: Only the resulting HTML is returned in the HTTP response.
mc.ez: 浏览器只收到结果 HTML。

mc.q: Which is a PHP web development framework?
mc.e: Laravel is for PHP; Django is Python; React/Vue are JavaScript.

mc.q: Which is NOT a benefit of using a web development framework?
o: Server-side validation is no longer needed
mc.e: Frameworks help with validation but data still must be validated on the server.
mc.ez: 框架不会令服务器验证变得不需要。

mc.q: Which statement about the <form> tag is correct?
o: It is displayed as a box on the page
Input elements must be placed inside the form tag pair to be submitted together
Its method attribute sets the file to receive the data
mc.e: All input elements must be placed within <form>...</form>.
mc.ez: 字段必须放在 form 内。

mc.q: Which attribute of <form> specifies the location to send the form's data?
mc.e: action = where the data goes.

mc.q: Which line is written correctly?
mc.e: <input> is an empty element with no closing tag.

mc.q: A text field has no name attribute. What happens when the form is submitted?
o: Its value is sent with the index "text"
Its value is sent with an empty index
It is not submitted, so the server cannot read it
The browser refuses to submit the form
mc.e: Fields without a name are not submitted.
mc.ez: 没有 name 的字段不会提交。

mc.q: Which field type obscures the user's input on screen?
mc.e: type="password" hides the characters on screen.

mc.q: Which statement about a password field is correct?
o: It encrypts the data before sending
It only hides the characters on screen
Its value cannot be read by PHP
It forces the form to use POST
mc.e: It does not encrypt; use POST and HTTPS.
mc.ez: 只在画面上遮盖，不加密。

mc.q: In what format is the value of <input type="date"> submitted?
mc.e: Date fields submit yyyy-mm-dd.

mc.q: Which attributes restrict the range of dates a user can pick in a date field?
mc.e: min and max constrain the range.

mc.q: <select name="r"><option value="KL">Kowloon</option></select>. The user picks Kowloon. What is submitted?
mc.e: The value attribute is submitted with the select's name as index.

mc.q: <select name="fruit"><option>Apple</option><option>Pear</option></select>. The user picks Pear. What is submitted?
mc.e: If value is omitted, the text between the option tags is submitted.
mc.ez: 没 value 就提交标签内文字。

mc.q: Where should the name attribute of a dropdown be placed?
mc.e: name goes on <select>.

mc.q: Why must checkboxes for one question have a name ending in [], e.g. hobby[]?
o: So that all ticked values are sent and collected as an array
To display them in a list
To make only one box tickable
mc.e: [] lets PHP collect multiple values into an array.

mc.q: A form has 3 checkboxes named lang[]; none are ticked. In the PHP script, isset($_POST["lang"]) returns:
mc.e: Unticked boxes send nothing, so the index does not exist.
mc.ez: 都没勾 → index 不存在 → false。

mc.q: <input type="submit" name="submit" value="Go!">. What does the value attribute do?
o: Sets the text displayed on the button
Sets the URL to submit to
mc.e: value changes the button's label (and is also the submitted value).

mc.q: Which attribute makes the browser block submission when a field is empty?
mc.e: required forces the user to fill in the field.

mc.q: <input type="number" name="w">. The user enters 81.3. What happens?
o: The browser blocks it because the default step is 1
mc.e: Default step is 1, so only whole numbers are valid.
mc.ez: 默认 step=1 只收整数。

mc.q: Which attribute value lets a number field accept any real number?
mc.e: step="any".

mc.q: A form must let users choose ONE delivery district from 18 fixed districts. The most suitable field is:
mc.e: Pre-defined single choice → dropdown, reduces error.

mc.q: When form data is submitted, which part becomes the index of each pair?
mc.e: name is the index; user input is the value.

mc.q: A form has no method attribute. Which method is used?
mc.e: Default is GET.

mc.q: A form has action="". Where is the data sent?
o: To the same URL as the current page
mc.e: Empty action → same URL.

mc.q: Which URL shows a correctly formed query string?
mc.e: Starts with ?, pairs index=value, separated by &.

mc.q: With POST, the form data is placed in:
mc.e: POST data goes in the request body.

mc.q: Who decides whether a form uses GET or POST?
o: The browser, based on data size
The web developer, through the method attribute
The web server, after receiving the data
mc.e: Misconception box: the developer decides.

mc.q: Which request is most suitable for GET?
o: Filtering products by brand and price
mc.e: Retrieving resources without changing the server.

mc.q: Which is a reason to use POST for a login form?
o: The password will not be shown in the address bar or saved in history
POST data is always encrypted even without HTTPS
mc.e: POST data is not visible and not bookmarked.

mc.q: Which statement about GET and HTTPS is correct?
o: With HTTPS, the request URL including the query string is encrypted during transmission
HTTPS only encrypts the request body
GET cannot be used with HTTPS
HTTPS shows the query string in plain text on the network
mc.e: HTTPS encrypts the whole request, URL included.
mc.ez: HTTPS 连 URL 都加密。

mc.q: What is the approximate maximum size of a GET query string in most cases?
mc.e: About 2KB.

mc.q: Which can be sent with POST but NOT with GET?
o: Binary data such as an image file
mc.e: GET only carries text data.

mc.q: Why can responses to GET requests be cached by a proxy server?
o: The same URL fetches the same resource, so a stored copy can be reused
GET requests have a request body
mc.e: GET fetches a resource identified by the URL.
mc.ez: 同一 URL 取同一资源可重用。

mc.q: "Sending the same request multiple times should not alter the server's state." This describes:
mc.e: Enrichment: GET is idempotent.

mc.q: A shared YouTube link opens the same video for everyone because:
o: It is a GET request whose parameters are in the URL
It is cached on the user's device
mc.e: The query string is in the URL, so it can be shared.
mc.ez: GET 参数在 URL 可分享。

mc.q: How many index-value pairs are in: book.php?id=7&lang=en&submit=go ?
mc.e: id, lang, submit.

mc.q: In PHP, POST form data is accessed through:
mc.e: $_POST superglobal.

mc.q: The URL is quiz.php?ans=B. Which PHP expression gives "B"?
mc.e: Query string data is in $_GET; index must be a string.

mc.q: A user enters 179 in a number field named height. What is the data type of $_POST["height"]?
mc.e: All form data arrives as strings.

mc.q: Checkboxes are named lang[]. Which PHP expression accesses the array of ticked values?
mc.e: The index has no brackets.

mc.q: Height 200 (cm), weight 80 (kg). $bmi = $_POST["weight"] / ($_POST["height"]/100) ** 2; What is $bmi?
What does echo "Hi {$_POST["name"]}!"; output if name is Mei?
mc.e: {} embeds the array element in a double-quoted string.

mc.q: $_POST["x"] is "7" and $_POST["y"] is "5". What does echo $_POST["x"] + $_POST["y"]; output?
mc.e: + converts numeric strings to numbers (. would concatenate).

mc.q: A form uses method="POST". The PHP page reads $_GET["name"]. What happens?
o: The index does not exist, as the data is in $_POST
It gets an empty string by design
The browser converts POST to GET
mc.e: POST data is not in $_GET.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of client-side validation?
o: It reduces the workload on the server
It can check whether a username is taken
It works the same on every browser
mc.e: It prevents most invalid data from being sent.

mc.q: Which check can ONLY be done by server-side validation?
o: Username has not already been registered
mc.e: Needs the server's database.

mc.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Use either client-side or server-side validation, not both
Client-side and server-side validation are used in parallel
Server-side validation is unnecessary if required is used
Client-side validation runs after data reaches the server
mc.e: Misconception box.

mc.q: Why should data be validated on the server even if the form has required, min and max?
o: The user can edit the HTML or send a fabricated HTTP request directly
HTML attributes slow down the browser
mc.e: Client-side validation can be bypassed.

mc.q: What does isset($_POST["age"]) return when the user submitted age as an empty string?
mc.e: The index exists (value ""), so isset is true.

mc.q: Which values make empty($x) return true?
mc.e: empty is true for missing, "", "0", 0, null, false, [].

mc.q: A user types the URL of resultBMI.php directly. The script contains echo $_POST["name"]; with no checks. What happens?
o: It shows the last name entered
A GET request is sent; the index does not exist and a runtime warning/error occurs
The browser shows the form again
mc.e: Typing the URL sends GET; $_POST is empty.

mc.q: What does strlen("Hong Kong") return?
mc.e: 9 characters including the space.

mc.q: What does strpos("tom@hk.com", "@") return?
mc.e: Positions start at 0: s0 a1 m2 @3.

mc.q: What does strpos("samhk.com", "@") return?
mc.e: Not found → false.

mc.q: Which check does in_array($_POST["size"], ["S","M","L"]) perform?
mc.e: Value must be one of a fixed set.

mc.q: Which of these makes is_numeric() return false?
mc.e: "12abc" is not a numeric string.

mc.q: $valid = true; if(empty($_POST["h"])){ $valid=false; } elseif($_POST["h"]<0 || $_POST["h"]>250){ $valid=false; }  With h = "260", $valid is:
mc.e: 260 > 250 fails the range check.

mc.q: Today is 2026-11-25. With if($_POST["d"] > date("Y-m-d")){ $valid=false; }, which d makes $valid false?
mc.e: Only a later date string is greater.

mc.q: $f = ["a","b","c"]; foreach($f as $x){ if(empty($_POST[$x])) $valid = false; } The purpose is:
o: Presence check on every expected field
mc.e: Loop presence check.

mc.q: Which validation is "email must contain @"?
mc.e: Pattern of the data → format check.

mc.q: A Cookie is best described as:
o: A file stored in the server's database
A small text file stored by a website on the client's browser
mc.e: Definition.
mc.ez: 客户端浏览器的小文本文件。

mc.q: How does a server ask the browser to create a Cookie?
o: By sending a set-cookie header in the HTTP response
By adding it to the query string
The browser creates it on its own
mc.e: set-cookie header in the response.

mc.q: Which superglobal reads Cookies in PHP?
mc.e: $_COOKIE.

mc.q: A Cookie set by abc.com is sent with:
o: every HTTP request to any domain
mc.e: Cookies are domain-specific and sent with every request to that domain.
